summary: This work demonstrates gate-based RF reflectometry on a large-area vertical 4H-SiC MOSFET (Wolfspeed CPM2-1200-0025A) with parasitic capacitances of order nanofarads, showing gate-dependent reflectometry response at room temperature near $f_0 \approx 566$ MHz but complete loss of sensitivity below $T \approx 45$ K despite maintained DC transport. The signal degradation at cryogenic temperatures is attributed to carrier freeze-out in the drift region increasing $R_\mathrm{drift}$ from sub-ohms to $\approx 8.6$ kΩ at 28 K, which redirects RF current through gate-independent parasitic capacitive paths and suppresses the current-participation factor governing reflectometry contrast.
motivation: RF reflectometry is the dominant readout technique for semiconductor qubits but has been limited to nanoscale devices with small capacitances; understanding reflectometry in the regime of large parasitic capacitances and complex impedance environments is essential for scaling to cryo-CMOS architectures with multiplexed control lines. Large-area vertical MOSFETs serve as a useful proxy for studying how parasitic pathways degrade RF readout sensitivity in densely integrated quantum systems.
method: Gate-based RF reflectometry was performed on a commercial SiC power MOSFET wire-bonded to a custom PCB with resonator inductor $L_r = 8$ nH, using local grounding at the PCB to suppress loom parasitics. DC transfer characteristics and reflection coefficient $S_{11}$ measurements were taken at room temperature and $T = 28$ K, with results modeled using lumped-element circuits including device capacitances ($C_\mathrm{GS} \approx 2$ nF, $C_\mathrm{GD} \approx 2$ nF) and temperature-dependent resistances. A modified circuit configuration with additional resonant capacitors and RF chokes at the source and drain was proposed to restore sensitivity at cryogenic temperatures.
result: At room temperature, $|\Delta S_{11}|$ peaks near $f_0$ with stronger response ($\approx 2-3\times$ larger) for $V_\mathrm{GS} < V_\mathrm{th}^\mathrm{RT} \approx 1.5$ V, indicating sensitivity to drift-region resistance modulation. At 28 K with $V_\mathrm{th}^\mathrm{cryo} \approx 6$ V and $R_\mathrm{DS,on}^\mathrm{cryo} \approx 110$ kΩ, the reflectometry contrast drops below the VNA noise floor ($< 10^{-3}$ in $|S_{11}|$) across the measurement bandwidth despite gate-controlled DC transport, whereas circuit simulations with $R_\mathrm{drift} = 8.6$ kΩ recover the observed loss of sensitivity.
